question: There are estimated to be between 15 000 and 30 000 stewards in Italy. The lack of clear regulation and a professional register certifying the exact number of stewards active in the country has led to uncertainty for this category of workers.

The profession of steward was established in 2007, but despite the passage of time, no measures have been taken to ensure more detailed regulation and appropriate professional recognition. It is important to highlight that stewards play a public service role and can therefore be compared to auxiliary police officers.

The lack of an official status makes stewards more vulnerable in case problems arise when performing their duties. Expanding the single professional card to include stewards would make it possible to establish uniform standards of professional qualification and competence, ensuring increased safety for both the stewards and the public at sports venues. In view of the above: 1.

Can the Commission consider the inclusion of this profession in the categories of workers eligible to be issued with the single professional card, in order to ensure a safe working environment for all workers in the sector?
Taking the Italian model as an example, does the Commission not plan to introduce an ad hoc standard for training new stewards through the Erasmus+ programme?
answer: The decision to regulate a particular profession is taken by a Member State by establishing legislation, regulatory or administrative provisions requiring possession of specific qualifications to access the profession.

The European Professional Card (EPC) is an electronic procedure that allows professionals to apply for the recognition of their qualifications to access certain regulated professions in another Member State. As such the EPC provides for a procedure for making an application.
Therefore, including the profession of steward in the EPC would not impact how the profession or its standards are regulated at national level, while the use of EPC can facilitate the recognition.

There are possibilities through Erasmus+ to develop vocational education and training curricula and qualifications such as the Centres of Vocational Excellence (CoVEs) initiative (1) which aims to be a driving force in the sector. The CoVEs initiative could be explored by organisations who wish to apply for a project to develop the skills of a specific sector.
There are open calls every year with specific eligibility and award criteria. For the time being no project covering the profession of stewards is funded.
